name: Netherlands
summary: EU citizens register with the municipality. The Dutch investor residence scheme (EUR 1.25 million) ended on 1 January 2024 and there is no passive-income or digital nomad permit. US citizens can use the Dutch-American Friendship Treaty (DAFT) to run a business with a EUR 4,500 investment. Others need an employer-sponsored permit such as the highly skilled migrant permit or the EU Blue Card (EUR 5,942 a month gross from age 30).
naturalisation: Five years of uninterrupted lawful residence on a qualifying permit (3 years living with a Dutch partner), civic integration exam at A2 (a rise to B1 was reported as planned or postponed; unclear). Fee about EUR 1,139 in 2026 (sources differ).
dual_citizenship_note: Applicants generally must renounce their other nationality, with exceptions (for example where renouncing causes serious financial loss, or the home country does not allow renunciation). Secondary sources.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register with the municipality (BRP) if staying over four months; no permit.

routes.name: Residence permit for foreign investors
routes.summary: Residence for investing EUR 1.25 million; ended on 1 January 2024.
routes.requirements: The scheme required at least EUR 1,250,000 invested in the Dutch economy (property excluded). Closed to new applications from 1 January 2024; existing permits stay valid but cannot be extended under this scheme.

routes.status_note: Abolished for new applications from 1 January 2024 (one trade site reported October 2023).

routes.name: Dutch-American Friendship Treaty (DAFT) self-employed permit
routes.summary: US citizens can get a two-year residence permit to run their own business with about EUR 4,500 invested.
routes.requirements: Only US nationals (a separate treaty exists for Japanese). Substantial capital investment in the business, usually EUR 4,500 (level depends on the business form), or a key position at a US company, or a free profession. Since 1 April 2024 the conditions must be met within six months after the permit is granted (Chamber of Commerce registration and investment). Initial permit 2 years, extension 5 years, with continuous genuine activity. Application fee EUR 423 in 2026; decision period 90 days. IND temporary procedure was due to be evaluated around 1 April 2026; status not confirmed.
routes.physical_presence: Live in the Netherlands and run the business actively

routes.family: Family can join; not sourced in detail.
routes.tax_note: Becoming a Dutch tax resident follows facts and circumstances, not the permit.

routes.name: Highly skilled migrant and EU Blue Card (work)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored permit for skilled workers, with a recognised sponsor.
routes.requirements: 2026 gross monthly salary (excluding holiday allowance): EUR 5,942 aged 30 or over, EUR 4,357 under 30, EUR 3,122 for recent graduates; EU Blue Card EUR 5,942 (EUR 4,754 reduced). Annual equivalent for age 30+: EUR 71,304. IND fee EUR 423 paid by the employer.
routes.fees_note: Employer pays the fee by direct debit.
routes.tax_note: The 30% ruling (reduced) may apply; not researched here.

open_questions: DAFT: whether the temporary procedure was extended after 1 April 2026, and years to permanent residence for DAFT holders.

No passive-income / financially independent or digital nomad permit was found on the IND site; search was not exhaustive. Also not covered: ordinary self-employed points system and start-up (mentor) permit.
